title: Finite equilibrium cooperativity cannot remove quadratic dilute pair occupancy
statement: For equilibrium weights (1,a,a,w a^2) with finite fixed w=exp(J/(RT)), Z=1+2a+w a^2, P11=w a^2/Z and per-site occupancy x=(a+w a^2)/Z. As a tends to zero, x/a tends to one and P11/x^2 tends to w. Finite fixed pair stabilization changes the prefactor, not the asymptotic order.

requires: dilute activity a tending to zero
provides: obstruction to a fixed-cooperativity first-order transfer
assumptions: fixed finite stabilization as concentration changes
equilibrium occupancy, not a protected non-equilibrium intermediate
no inference of a measured catalyst binding energy
costs: A kinetic persistence route requires separately acquired survival/arrival/readout rates; not supplied by stronger equilibrium binding.
contract.units: a, x, P11 and w dimensionless; J and RT in common molar-energy units
contract.obstruction: Stops finite equilibrium pair enhancement from being substituted for the scale-separated persistent-capture operation.

evidence.quote: Finite, fixed adsorption cooperativity cannot eliminate the quadratic dependence of equilibrium pair formation on sufficiently dilute reactant activity.

review.scope: Exact equilibrium model and its stated dilute-limit obstruction.
